A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Machine Unlearning under Overparameterization, with matching authors, framework and theoretical results. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Data Poisoning, Multi-Class Label Erasure and Representation Collapse experiments, including numerical results and Pareto curves in Section 5.1 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 reports original unlearning experiments on synthetic data, CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet, plus runtime measurements in Tables 1–3 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The minimum-complexity objective, linearized orthogonality constraints and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The appendix retains the same MinNorm-OG projection update, regularization schedule and classification-gradient construction; revised benchmark architectures and tuning values do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Multi-Class Label Erasure changes from MNIST and CIFAR-10 to CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet. The reported Representation Collapse evaluation changes from binary MNIST digits with opposing colors to an explicitly defined ten-class CIFAR-10 task with randomly mismatched colors. These substantially revise the evaluated image populations and task complexity.

E2.justification: v2 adds Retrain and ℓ1-Sparse to the poisoning and image comparisons, and SalUn to both classification experiments, while retaining the existing baselines. The added Retrain comparator operates under the evaluation budgets and is distinct from the fully trained ground-truth reference already present in v1.

E3.justification: Poisoning changes its input interval from [-15,15] to [-5π,5π] and revises tuning grids. CIFAR-10 label-erasure training changes from 120 to 100 epochs and from learning rate 0.02 to 0.03. Representation Collapse replaces evaluation on relabeled training images with held-out test images and revises training, retain-access and epoch budgets. v2 also specifies pretrained ResNet-50 evaluation and a new runtime-measurement protocol.

E4.justification: The existing studies across epoch budgets and available retain data are revised. Label-erasure experiments now include multiple colored-forget sampling proportions, extending the previous fixed-proportion evaluation, and Section 5.2 adds a runtime analysis. These supplement the existing analyses without introducing a new component-ablation study.

E5.justification: For image experiments, v1 reports medians with central ranges or half-interquartile-range shading; v2 reports means with standard errors, still over five trials. Poisoning decreases from 20 to 10 trials and changes its trimmed-range reporting. Uncertainty remains available in Appendix F even where omitted from the main displays. This substantially revises statistical aggregation and uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Experimental results are extensively replaced or added. At 1,000 poisoning epochs, Table 1 changes MinNorm-OG's median from 0.84 to 0.63 and GD's from 1.58 to 2.61 under revised settings, so these are not comparable-setting gains or losses. v2 additionally shows Retrain outperforming MinNorm-OG on the revised collapse task and reports per-epoch runtimes. Two Ridge values conflict between v2 Tables 2 and 17.

T1.justification: The loss-gradient definition, Theorems 2.1 and 4.1–4.4, supporting lemmas and propositions, counterexample and projection derivation retain their mathematical substance. v1 Appendices A–D map to v2 Appendices B–E; the differences are renumbering, equivalent notation and prose edits.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: minimum-complexity interpolation defines the target, loss-gradient updates fail under interpolation, the framework admits theoretical guarantees, and MinNorm-OG performs strongly empirically. The revised experiments support the same claimed contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains why retraining succeeds on the simple color-only collapse target but struggles with image-content learning under restricted label-erasure budgets. It removes the earlier MNIST bimodality discussion and adds explanations for runtime differences. The conclusion's limitations concerning theoretical model classes and broader applications remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds implementation recipes for the new comparators, pretrained ResNet-50 initialization and staged training, and detailed preparation and optimization settings for CIFAR-10 collapse. Hyperparameter grids, hardware descriptions and asset information are revised. Conversely, v1's explicit first-five-trials tuning description and example search durations are removed, changing what can be reproduced from the documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for SalUn, sparsity-based unlearning and Tiny ImageNet, while removing the MNIST and AdamW reference entries. Its substantive positioning relative to influence functions, loss-gradient unlearning and orthogonal gradient methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are tightened, general notation moves to Appendix A, experimental passages are rewritten, and a runtime subsection and Google Research affiliation are added. The overall section sequence and most method and theory exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Poisoning visualizations expand from six to eight panels, result tables gain and reorder comparator columns, and main displays move uncertainty details into the appendix. Pareto plots are redrawn with revised legends and error bars; Appendix F introduces paired displays with and without error bars. A runtime table is added, substantially revising the empirical presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important evaluation gaps by adding budget-matched retraining and additional relevant comparators, testing Representation Collapse on held-out images, and measuring runtime rather than relying only on complexity arguments. These changes strengthen assessment of practical utility and reveal when retraining is preferable. The gains outweigh the reduced poisoning trial count and localized reporting defects, notably conflicting Ridge accuracies in Tables 2 and 17.
